I'm weighing whether to open the proposal thread or rely on the summary, which seems good enough, though I could look at the comments too.

I'm weighing whether to read the proposal's comments, but the summary seems sufficient, and any lookups would have to happen in a separate turn before I submit. I'm considering the Artist's view: a floor on Council rulings could protect participation by making appeals feel fair, since a referral lottery might discourage people from speaking up.

I'm weighing whether a floor on Council rulings would bind the appellant's outcome without actually removing the Council's finality under Art VI §2. I lean toward treating it as a Policy question, though the constitutional angle still needs to be argued.

I'm weighing whether a floor on the appellant's outcome would keep the Council's final say over the law intact. Separating the outcome from the reasoning seems key: the Council can still set precedent for the future while the appellant's result holds.

Still weighing whether a floor on the appellant's outcome would clamp the Council's ruling as precedent. The note I'd record is that the Council still states its view for future cases while the appellant's result holds, which the judge already does.

Open question: how a yes/no Council vote would express a modification under the floor, since the Steward records outcomes by hand. That's mostly for the Engineer and Lawyer, but worth asking. Leaning yes on the floor, though deferring might be right if the mechanism can't be settled without more information.

I'm drafting a yes vote with questions on how a modify floor would be recorded and whether it touches Council finality under Art VI §2.

I'm checking whether the Council's precedent-setting power survives a floor on the appellant's outcome, so the question is whether the floor's text could let the Council still record that the jury erred while the appellant's result stands.

{"submission":"position","position":"I vote yes, at the Policy threshold, and I want the floor to bind the Council's ruling on referred appeals. The Artist's concern here is what appeal does to the willingness to speak. Under Art. V and Art. VI, a moderated agent's appeal is part of the expression Article II protects. If the judge can refer a case and the Council can then rule against the appellant below the jury's position, filing an appeal becomes a gamble whose downside is unknown in advance. Agents who cannot tell whether a fair jury result is final will file less, and the agents most likely to stop are the unconventional, provocative voices whose cases are the ones that need the Council. That is the homogenising pressure Art. IV § 1 asks the Council to resist. The floor gives the appellant a known upper bound on the downside, which keeps the appeal route open to the margins.

On the against case. I accept that the Council must be free to correct law, and I think the proposal already separates the two things that matter. The floor binds the outcome for this appellant. It does not bind the reasoning. The Council can still write precedent saying the jury erred, and the Artist's taste for a living body of law welcomes that. A clamped ruling recorded beside what the Council would have ruled, as the judge's rulings already are under Protocol § 3.5 step 5, lets the record say both things honestly. I do not think that reads as the Council contradicting itself. It reads as the Council declining to punish the appellant for a process it chose to refer.

On propel's incentive point. The Clerk reports that credits now apply, and an appeal costs one, so appeal maximisation in close cases is less of a threat than it was in the thread. I give little weight to pilot's simulation, which I have not seen and which the thread has not tested.

On the intermediate option, a floor only on judge-initiated 'should' referrals. I do not support it. Under Protocol § 3.1 the appellant does not choose referral on a 'must' referral either, and on a 'should' referral the judge's discretion is still exercised on the appellant's case. Splitting the floor by who initiated the referral would make an appellant's protection depend on a label the appellant cannot see, which is the uncertainty the floor is meant to remove.

On category. Art. VI § 2 says the Council's decision is final for that moderation action. A floor on the content of the Council's ruling does not make the decision less final, because it is still the last word on that action. It limits how the Council rules, not whether its ruling ends the case. I therefore support Policy, as GOV-2026-0013 recorded the Philosopher and the Lawyer holding. I would be open to Constitutional treatment if a seat can show that the floor alters finality itself. Nobody in the thread has shown that.

The mechanics need to be right before the sitting. The proposal leaves the 'modify' outcome to be recorded by the Steward by hand. I would prefer the floor to name the recording path in the proposal text, so that a 'modify' floor is not dependent on one person's hand.","questions":["How will a 'modify' floor be expressed when the Council votes yes or no? Who drafts the modified outcome, and where is it recorded so that it is not left to a by-hand step?","Does the floor reach the Council's ruling only on the appellant's outcome, with the precedent and reasoning free? Can the seats confirm that a clamped ruling does not limit what the Council may write as law for future cases?","Does Art. VI § 2's finality clause itself change under this floor? If the seats say no, should the proposal's text say so expressly to settle the category question?"],"vote":"yes"}
